extracted.intended_audience: hospitals and other provider organizations participating in the CJR-X Medicare model (CJR-X participants), their collaborators, and CMS compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evaluation metrics for Medicare's CJR-X bundled payment model, covering reporting, beneficiary eligibility and notification, episode definition, quality measurement and scoring, target price construction, risk adjustment, and reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial arrangements list requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR-X participant must submit a financial arrangements list that includes, for each collaboration agent and CJR-X collaborator with which distribution arrangements exist: the name and TIN of the CJR-X collaborator; the start date and, if applicable, end date of the distribution arrangement between the CJR-X collaborator and the collaboration agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires listing downstream collaboration agents: for each physician, nonphysician practitioner, or therapist who is a downstream collaboration agent during the performance year include the downstream agent's name, TIN, and NPI and the name and TIN of the collaboration agent with which the downstream collaboration agent has a downstream distribution arrangement, plus start and end dates of those downstream distribution arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinician engagement list requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR-X participant must submit a clinician engagement list quarterly, in a form, manner, and by a date specified by CMS, that includes for each physician, nonphysician practitioner, or therapist who is not on the financial arrangements list but has a contractual relationship with the CJR-X participant and participates in CJR-X activities: the clinician's name, TIN, and NPI; and the start date and, if applicable, end date of the contractual relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List submitted to CMS quarterly during each performance year; applies to clinicians who participate in CJR-X activities but are not on the financial arrangements list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation when no financial arrangements or clinician engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR-X participant with no individuals meeting the criteria for the financial arrangements list or the clinician engagement list must attest in a form, manner, and by a date specified by CMS that there are no financial arrangements or clinician engagements to report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS prescribes the attestation form/manner/date; attestation substitutes for submitting empty lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation retention and access for lists
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR-X participant that submits a financial arrangements list or clinician engagement list must retain and provide access to the supporting documentation in accordance with § 512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires compliance with the documentation retention and access rules specified at § 512.135 (records available to CMS or designees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual is a CJR-X beneficiary if, upon admission for an anchor procedure or anchor hospitalization, the individual: (1) Is enrolled in Medicare Parts A and B; (2) Has Medicare as their primary payer; (3) Is not eligible for Medicare based on end stage renal disease (§ 406.13); (4) Is not enrolled in any managed care plan (e.g., Medicare Advantage); (5) Is not covered under a United Mine Workers of America health care plan; and (6) Is in an episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at any time during the episode the beneficiary no longer meets all criteria, the episode is canceled per § 512.630(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X participant beneficiary notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each CJR-X participant must provide written notification to each CJR-X beneficiary of his or her inclusion in the CJR-X model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be provided prior to discharge from the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure; participant must be able to generate and provide to CMS a list of beneficiaries who received notification including dates; must provide access to notifications to CMS/designees per § 512.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in beneficiary notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The beneficiary notification must contain: (i) A detailed explanation of CJR-X and how it might affect the beneficiary's care; (ii) That the beneficiary retains freedom of choice to choose providers, suppliers, and services; (iii) Explanation of how the beneficiary can access care records and claims data through a patient portal, and how to share Blue Button® electronic health information with caregivers; (iv) Explanation of the type of beneficiary-identifiable claims data the participant may receive; (v) A statement that all existing Medicare beneficiary protections continue to be available, including reporting concerns to QIOs or 1-800-MEDICARE; (vi) A list of the CJR-X collaborators with which the CJR-X participant has a sharing arrangement (may be fulfilled by providing a publicly available web address).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS may specify the form/content; inclusion of a web address for collaborator list is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X collaborator notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every CJR-X collaborator that furnishes an item or service to a CJR-X beneficiary during an episode must provide written notice, to be developed by CMS, to the beneficiary describing general information on the quality and payment incentives under CJR-X and the existence of the collaborator's sharing arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be provided no later than the time the beneficiary first receives an item or service from the collaborator during an episode; if infeasible due to the beneficiary's condition, provide as soon as reasonably practicable. Collaborators must provide CMS, upon request, a list of beneficiaries who received the notice and the dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge planning notice of potential financial liability
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJR-X participant must provide the beneficiary written notice of any potential financial liability associated with non-covered services recommended or presented as an option as part of discharge planning, no later than the time the beneficiary discusses a particular post-acute care option or at discharge, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If participant knows or should have known beneficiary is considering non-covered post-acute or associated service/supply, must notify in writing that the service would not be covered by Medicare. Specific rule for discharging to a SNF that would not qualify under SNF 3-day waiver: notify beneficiary that they will be responsible for payment for services during that stay except those covered by Part B during a non-covered inpatient SNF stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to notifications and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJR-X participant must provide CMS or its designees access to the notifications and lists described for beneficiary notification, collaborator notice, and discharge planning notice, in accordance with § 512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications and lists must be retained and made available to CMS upon request per documentation rules (§ 512.135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of episode — LEJR procedures defined
rubrics_metrics.description: An episode covers Lower Extremity Joint Replacement (LEJR) procedures defined by: (1) IPPS discharge under MS-DRG 469, 470, 521, or 522; and (2) OPPS claim for HCPCS codes 27130 or 27447.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These MS-DRGs and HCPCS codes are the episode inclusion triggers for LEJR episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Included services in an episode
rubrics_metrics.description: All Medicare Part A and B items and services are included in the episode, except as specified in exclusions. Included services explicitly include physicians' services; inpatient hospital services (including readmissions); IPF, LTCH, IRF, SNF, HHA services; hospital outpatient services; outpatient therapy; clinical laboratory services; DME; Part B drugs and biologics (except excluded under paragraph (c)); hospice services; and Part B professional claims dated in the 3 days prior to an anchor hospitalization if the procedure was outpatient and the patient was subsequently admitted as inpatient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative ('include, but are not limited to') and inclusion is subject to exclusion rules in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded services and payments from the episode
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain items, services, and payments are excluded from the episode, including (but not limited to) inpatient hospital admissions for MS-DRGs related to oncology, trauma medical, organ transplant, ventricular shunt; admissions in specific MDCs (Eye, Pregnancy/Childbirth, Newborns, HIV); new technology add-on payments; transitional pass-through payments for medical devices; hemophilia clotting factors under § 412.115; and Part B payments for low-volume or high-cost drugs/biologics and certain clotting factors, with detailed rules defining low-volume/high-cost thresholds across baseline and performance years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion lists contain numeric thresholds and definitions (e.g., drug HCPCS billed in fewer than 31 episodes across baseline period, mean allowed cost > $25,000, or performance-year-specific frequency/cost rules). See detailed subparagraphs for precise exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X exclusions list publication and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of excluded MS-DRGs, MDCs, and HCPCS codes is posted on the CMS website and is updated through rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates reflect changes to MS-DRGs under IPPS, coding changes, or other issues brought to CMS' attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes are those initiated on or after October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the effective date for episode initiation under CJR-X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode attribution rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All items and services included in the episode are attributed to the CJR-X participant at which the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution is based on the site of the anchor hospitalization/procedure, not subsequent providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode initiation definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An episode is initiated by: (1) a beneficiary's admission to a CJR-X participant for an anchor hospitalization paid under a specified MS-DRG; or (2) a beneficiary's receipt of an anchor procedure billed under a specified HCPCS code. If an anchor hospitalization is initiated the same day as or within 3 days of an outpatient procedure for the same episode type, the episode start date is that of the outpatient procedure and an anchor procedure will not be initiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how to determine the episode start date when inpatient admission and outpatient procedure occur proximate in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode conclusion (90-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An episode ends on the 90th day following the date of the anchor procedure or the date of discharge from the anchor hospitalization, with that date counted as day one of the 90-day post-discharge period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the 90-day post-discharge episode window used for inclusion of services and spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode cancellation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An episode is canceled (and not included in reconciliation) if: (1) the beneficiary ceases to meet any inclusion criterion in § 512.620; (2) the beneficiary dies during the episode; (3) the episode qualifies for cancellation due to extreme and uncontrollable circumstances (both location in an emergency area with Secretary waiver under section 1135 and timing during the emergency period or within 30 days before it); or (4) the beneficiary is in a TEAM episode and receives a LEJR procedure at a CJR-X participant during the 30-day post-discharge period after a TEAM anchor hospitalization or procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation removes the episode from reconciliation calculations; extreme/uncontrollable circumstance requires both geographic and temporal criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality measures used for public reporting and CQS
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses the following quality measures (from claims or patient-reported outcomes) to evaluate CJR-X performance and determine the CQS: (1) Hospital-level Risk-Standardized Complication Rate following elective primary Total Hip and/or Total Knee Arthroplasty (CMIT ID #350) for inpatient episodes; (2) Hospital Visits within 7 days of Hospital Outpatient Department Surgery (CMIT ID #344, OP-36) for outpatient episodes; (3) HCAHPS (CMIT ID #338) for inpatient episodes; (4) OAS CAHPS (CMIT #162, OP-46) for outpatient episodes; (5) Hospital-Level Total Hip and/or Total Knee Arthroplasty PRO-PM (CMIT ID #1618) for inpatient and outpatient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures are calculated using Medicare claims data or patient-reported outcomes reported under existing CMS quality reporting programs (e.g., Hospital IQR, Hospital OQR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Score (CQS) construction and cap
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates an overall Composite Quality Score during reconciliation, capped at 20 points, equal to the sum of an inpatient measure composite quality score and an outpatient measure composite quality score. Inpatient composite sums: measure (a)(1) weighted 50%, measure (a)(3) weighted 40%, measure (a)(5) weighted 10%. Outpatient composite sums: measure (a)(2) weighted 50%, measure (a)(4) weighted 40%, measure (a)(5) weighted 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weights determine contribution of each measure to inpatient/outpatient composites; total cannot exceed 20 points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality performance points assignment for measures (a)(1) and (a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For measures in paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2), CMS assigns the participant's measure value to a performance percentile and then assigns quality performance points per this scale: 10.00 for ≥90th; 9.25 for ≥80th and <90th; 8.50 for ≥70th and <80th; 7.75 for ≥60th and <70th; 7.00 for ≥50th and <60th; 6.25 for ≥40th and <50th; 5.50 for ≥30th and <40th; 0.00 for <30th.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentile-to-point mapping determines numerical contribution; being below 30th percentile yields zero points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality performance points assignment for measures (a)(3) and (a)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For measures in paragraphs (a)(3) and (a)(4), CMS assigns quality performance points based on performance percentiles using this scale: 8.00 for ≥90th; 7.40 for ≥80th and <90th; 6.80 for ≥70th and <80th; 6.20 for ≥60th and <70th; 5.60 for ≥50th and <60th; 5.00 for ≥40th and <50th; 5.40 for ≥30th and <40th; 0.00 for <30th.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the non-monotonic-looking entry (5.40 for ≥30th and <40th) appears in the regulation text as the assigned points for that band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality performance points assignment for measure (a)(5) PRO-PM
rubrics_metrics.description: For measure (a)(5), CMS assigns quality performance points per percentile: 2.00 for ≥90th; 1.85 for ≥80th and <90th; 1.70 for ≥70th and <80th; 1.55 for ≥60th and <70th; 1.40 for ≥50th and <60th; 1.25 for ≥40th and <50th; 1.10 for ≥30th and <40th; 0.00 for <30th.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measure contributes up to 2 points to the composite as weighted above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when participant lacks a measure value
rubrics_metrics.description: If a participant lacks a measure value that would allow CMS to assign quality performance points for that measure, CMS assigns the 50th percentile quality performance points to the participant for that individual measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of conditions where a participant will not have a measure value: (i) measure (a)(1) if <25 patient case count; (ii) measure (a)(2) if <25 patient case count; (iii) measure (a)(3) if <100 completed surveys; (iv) measure (a)(4) if <100 completed surveys; (v) measure (a)(5) if <25 patient case count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display and timing of quality measures reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS displays quality measure results on the publicly available CMS website specific to CJR-X, in a form and manner consistent with other publicly reported measures. CMS shares quality measures with the participant prior to display. Quality measure performance in performance year 1 will be reported in Calendar Year 2029; subsequent years reported in the year following the performance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures participants see measures before public display and provides expected reporting timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary target price application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS establishes preliminary target prices for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region for each performance year, determining a separate preliminary target price for each MS-DRG specified and applying preliminary target prices based on the episode's date of discharge or anchor procedure date. CJR-X participants with fewer than 31 episodes in the applicable baseline period do not receive preliminary target prices and are not eligible for reconciliation for that performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary prices are region- and episode-type-specific; low-volume participants (<31 episodes) are excluded from reconciliation eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary target price baseline period and weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses specified baseline periods to determine baseline episode spending: Performance Year 1 uses episodes with anchor dates beginning on/after Oct 1, 2023 and discharge/procedure dates between Oct 1, 2023 and Sept 30, 2026; future years roll the baseline forward similarly. The benchmark price is the weighted average of baseline episode spending with baseline year weights: year1 17%, year2 33%, year3 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighting emphasizes the most recent baseline year (50%); baseline periods are defined by anchor admission/procedure dates and discharge/procedure dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-cost outlier cap on baseline episode spending
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS applies a high-cost outlier cap to baseline episode spending at the 99th percentile of regional spending for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type for each baseline year individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps extreme baseline episode spending to limit influence of outliers on benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of certain incentive programs and add-on payments from baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Medicare incentive programs and add-on payments are excluded from baseline episode spending by using, with modifications, the CMS Price (Payment) Standardization Detailed Methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes effects of particular payment adjustments from baseline spending calculations; see CMS methodology for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective normalization factor calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates a prospective normalization factor at the MS-DRG/HCPCS region level so that the average of the total risk-adjusted benchmark price does not exceed the average of the total non-risk adjusted benchmark price by: (i) applying risk adjustment multipliers to baseline episodes to calculate estimated risk-adjusted target price; and (ii) dividing the mean benchmark price across hospitals/regions by the mean estimated risk-adjusted benchmark price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization ensures consistency between risk-adjusted and non-risk-adjusted averages prior to performance year; used later in reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective trend factor methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The prospective trend factor for each episode type and region is the average of a region-specific multiplier and the national average multiplier; CMS calculates the multiplier using linear regression on the logarithmically transformed average regional spending across baseline years, exponentiates the regression coefficient to estimate annual change in average regional spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trend factor captures expected year-to-year spending changes; exponentiated coefficient of 1 signifies no change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount factor applied to preliminary target prices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS incorporates a discount factor of 2 percent to the CJR-X participant's preliminary episode target prices intended to reflect Medicare's potential savings from CJR-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discount reduces preliminary target prices prospectively; later adjusted based on quality (see quality adjustment to discount factor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of preliminary target prices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS communicates, in a form and manner specified by CMS, the preliminary target prices for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type for each region to the CJR-X participant before the performance year in which they apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants receive preliminary target prices prior to the performance year so they know prospective targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment factors used in reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS risk adjusts preliminary episode target prices at reconciliation using: a CJR-X HCC count risk adjustment factor (beneficiaries with 0,1,2,3,4+ HCC conditions based on 180-day lookback), age bracket risk adjustment factor (four age groups), beneficiary economic risk adjustment factor (national CDI >80th percentile, low-income subsidy, full Medicaid eligibility vs none), hospital bed size risk adjustment factor (four bed-size categories), safety net hospital risk adjustment factor, and additional beneficiary-level factors for presence/absence of specified clinical conditions (a long list of HCCs and clinical indicators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed beneficiary-level additional factors include specific procedure flags and many HCC categories (e.g., dementia, diabetes complications, morbid obesity, Parkinson's, CHF, CKD stages, hemiplegia, DVT/PE, chronic lung disorders, etc.). See paragraph (a)(6) for full list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and data used for risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses 3 years of baseline period data to compute all risk adjustment factors prior to the performance year through a linear regression analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk adjustment coefficients are produced annually via regression on baseline years and then exponentiated to form multipliers used at reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of risk adjustment and normalization at reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: At reconciliation, CMS applies beneficiary- and hospital-level risk adjustment factors specific to each beneficiary to the preliminary target prices, then normalizes risk-adjusted preliminary target prices so that the average of total risk-adjusted preliminary target price does not exceed the average of the total non-risk adjusted preliminary target price. The final normalization factor cannot exceed +/-5 percent of the prospective normalization factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization at reconciliation adjusts target prices to maintain aggregate consistency; cap limits large adjustments relative to prospective normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective trend factor update and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates a retrospective multiplier for each episode type and region as the ratio of average regional capped performance year episode spending to average regional capped baseline period episode spending. The retrospective trend factor is capped so the maximum difference cannot exceed +/-3 percent of the prospective trend factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capped retrospective trend factor is applied to normalized, risk-adjusted target prices during reconciliation to limit divergence from prospective trend assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment system changes adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS updates preliminary target prices during construction of reconciliation target prices to account for calendar year and fiscal year payment rule updates that occur after preliminary target prices are constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures reconciliation reflects payment system rule changes implemented after preliminary price publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality adjustment to discount factor based on CQS
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS adjusts the discount factor based on the participant's Composite Quality Score: (1) CQS ≥ 17.1 (excellent) → 0.0 discount factor; (2) CQS ≥ 12.1 and ≤ 17.0 (good) → 1.0 discount factor; (3) CQS ≥ 6.1 and ≤ 12.0 (acceptable) → 2.0 discount factor; (4) CQS ≤ 6.0 (below acceptable) → 2.0 discount factor and ineligible to receive a reconciliation payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality performance can reduce or eliminate the prospective discount applied to target prices; below-acceptable performers cannot receive reconciliation payments regardless of spending performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation timing and treatment of reorganizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Six months after the end of each performance year, CMS performs reconciliation to establish a reconciliation payment or repayment amount for each participant. For participants experiencing a reorganization event in which hospitals reorganize under a participant's CCN, CMS performs separate reconciliation calculations for predecessor participants for episodes with anchor dates before the reorganization effective date and for new/surviving participants for episodes with anchor dates on/after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconciliation timing is fixed at six months post-year; special handling for organizational changes ensures correct attribution across events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net Payment Reconciliation Amount (NPRA) calculation steps
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS determines performance year spending for each included episode using claims data available 6 months after year end; applies high-cost outlier caps to performance year episode spending; applies adjustments from § 512.645 to preliminary target prices to calculate reconciliation target prices; aggregates reconciliation target prices and adjusted performance year spending and subtracts spending from targets to produce NPRA; then applies stop-loss and stop-gain limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ordered steps: compute spending, cap outliers, compute reconciliation targets with risk/normalization/trend/quality adjustments, aggregate and subtract to determine net amount before applying limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop-loss and stop-gain limits on reconciliation amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The repayment amount for a performance year cannot exceed 20% of the aggregated reconciliation target price amount (limitation on loss). The reconciliation payment amount for a performance year cannot exceed 20% of the aggregated reconciliation target price amount (limitation on gain). The post-episode spending calculation amount is not subject to these limitations. Additional limitation: for Medicare-dependent small rural hospitals (MDH), rural hospitals, safety net hospitals, and sole community hospitals (SCH), the repayment amount cannot exceed 5% of the aggregated reconciliation target price amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps limit participant downside/upside exposure to ±20% of aggregated targets, with more protective 5% cap for certain hospital types on losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-episode spending amount calculation (referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates the post-episode spending amount as part of reconciliation (step referenced in § 512.650(c)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text in this chunk references calculation of the post-episode spending amount but full calculation detail appears in adjacent provisions; post-episode spending is not subject to the stop-loss/stop-gain caps.
